issues.body: The module says rewriting the adopted mask preserves the verdict unless the adversary guesses secret r, and the test adds a blind fixed delta. But malicious_secure_equal_batch obtains r from session.draw_nonzero_fp() under the same ShamirDealer/MacSession whose corruption defines this residual. That dealer knows mask_value and can rewrite every mask value share by delta = -r. The adopted operand is then a valid sharing of zero; auth_mul produces product d*0 and a consistent carried MAC, so mac_check_and_open accepts and any unequal pair becomes equal. Thus the corrupt-dealer hardening/verdict-preservation claim remains false, and the current test is vacuous for the actual adversary described.
issues.fix_hint: Remove the claims that operand order hardens against a corrupt dealer and that a dealer must guess r. Replace corrupt_dealer_rewrite_of_the_mask_preserves_the_verdict with a residual-attack witness using delta = mask.neg() and assert that an unequal verdict flips while the MAC check accepts, or redesign randomness so the rewriting adversary genuinely cannot know r. Keep the Malicious descriptor explicitly limited to <=t corrupt parties with an honest trusted dealer and retain the research-grade/external-audit caveat. Update the matching skill and research text consistently.
issues.title: Corrupt dealer still knows the mask and can zero the adopted operand

verdict.summary: Round 4 is stagnant: the round-3 major soundness/honesty issue remains materially unchanged. The implementation draws the equality mask through the same in-process ShamirDealer/MacSession, while the documentation and test assume a corrupt dealer must choose its rewrite blindly because it does not know r. A corrupt dealer knows the mask it generated and can consistently rewrite the adopted second operand by delta = -r, producing r' = 0. auth_mul then carries a matching product/MAC for d*0, mac_check_and_open accepts, and an unequal pair is returned as equal. The fixed +9 test does not exercise this load-bearing residual. The <=t-party claim may remain separately scoped, but the corrupt-dealer hardening and verdict-preservation claims must be removed or corrected.
